items.title: an assignment whose left side is not a place — `-x = 1;`, `!b = true;`, `(x + 1) = 2;`, `await x = 1;`, `async (x) = 1;` — passes `vilan check` and the JS backend emits an invalid left-hand side (`SyntaxError: Invalid left-hand side in assignment` at load)
items.discussion: syntax-46 (Order 46); REPORT-syntax-46.md; B494 (which made `async x = 1;` a parse-level steer, the one spelling a person plausibly writes)
items.body: Repro on v0.43.0 (fe092e8d): `fun main() { mut x = 0; (x + 1) = 2; -x = 1; print(x); }` checks clean; `vilan run` throws at load (`x + 1 = 2;` in the emitted module). `parsing::Parser::parse_assignment` takes any struct-free precedence chain as the place and only checks that an assignment operator follows; nothing downstream refuses a non-place. `async x += 1;` happens to be refused by the operator check (`Promise` has no `Add`), which is how B494's shape surfaced. Rec: refuse at the parser with a steer naming what a place is (a name, a member, an index, a `*` deref — and a tuple of places if the language admits one), so both backends are covered; or in the analyzer's assignment arm. Native untested. Sizing S–M.

items.title: a bare `return;` (and `return (x);`, `return -x;`, a block's tail `{ return }`) still says "cannot find 'return' in this scope" — each is a VALID parse (a read of a binding named `return`, a call, a subtraction), so B520's parser steer cannot reach it; the analyzer's unresolved-name path should add it
items.body: B520 steers `return value` where no name can stand. `return;` with `let return = 1;` in scope is a valid program today (it reads the binding and discards it), so the parser must leave it a name; only resolution knows the name is unbound. Rec: in the analyzer's 'cannot find' path (`import_steer` or beside it), when the unresolved name is `return`, append "vilan spells this `ret`" and let the editor's B520 fix (`parsing::foreign_spelling_fix` keys on the message) offer the rewrite; the same for a call `fn(..)`/`function(..)`/`def(..)` only if a probe shows it is common. `parsing::ForeignSpelling` is public for this. analyzer.rs is solver-b-46's file. Sizing S.

items.title: `macro async fun` parses and `async macro fun` does not, though B485 Q8's written order puts `async` before `macro`; is an async macro meaningful at all?
items.discussion: syntax-46 (Order 46); keywords-vs-attributes.md Q8; marker census I1/I3/M1
items.body: B486's canonicalizer leaves a keyword set it does not list as legal exactly as written, and `async`+`macro` is not listed, so today's behaviour stands (census: `macro` < `async`, one order only). Doors: (a) an async macro is not a thing — refuse both orders with a steer; (b) it is — admit the ruled order `async macro fun`, steer the other, and teach the printer. Rec: (a), unless the macro engine has a use. Sizing XS.
